title: Rethinking Activation Functions: Reducing Bias Can Improve Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.14500v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Many widely used activation functions, including ReLU, GELU, Swish, and Sigmoid, produce predominantly positive outputs, resulting in a nonzero post-activation mean that we term activation bias. Despite its ubiquity, the effect of activation bias on learning dynamics remains poorly understood. Using controlled models, we show that activation bias accelerates initial loss reduction but is accompanied by overshooting, non-smooth trajectories, and a steeper loss landscape. This early advantage also coincides with the model's use of task-relevant information encoded in the activation bias component. In contrast, reducing activation bias slows initial learning but ultimately yields a lower final loss. Experiments on larger vision and language models exhibit a similar pattern: smaller activation bias is associated with better late-stage performance. translated_title: 重新思考激活函数：减少偏置可以改善学习
translated_abstract: 许多广泛使用的激活函数，包括ReLU、GELU、Swish和Sigmoid，产生的输出以正值为主，导致激活后均值非零，我们将其称为“激活偏置”。尽管激活偏置普遍存在，但其对学习动力学的影响仍知之甚少。通过受控模型，我们证明激活偏置加速了初始损失的下降，但伴随着过冲、不平滑的轨迹以及更陡峭的损失景观。这种早期优势也与模型利用编码在激活偏置分量中的任务相关信息相吻合。相反，减少激活偏置会减缓初始学习，但最终能获得更低的损失。在更大规模的视觉和语言模型上的实验显示出类似的模式：更小的激活偏置与更好的后期性能相关。因此，这个看似微小的特性能实质性地改变学习进程，值得予以明确的关注。
tldr: 研究揭示了激活函数正值输出带来的“激活偏置”虽能加速初期学习，但减少该偏置反而能获得更低的最终损失和更好的后期性能。
en_tdlr: Reducing activation bias slows initial learning but ultimately achieves lower final loss, revealing that this overlooked property of activation functions substantially shapes learning dynamics and deserves explicit consideration.
